title: Temurah 11
description: Rabbi Zeira keeps defending bar Padda’s view that a fetus cannot be consecrated, the Gemara weighs it against baraitot on a live fetus found in a sin offering and on Rabbi Eliezer’s animals that are “neither sacred nor sanctify,” and then turns to one who consecrates a single limb: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon, three amora’im on vital limbs, and Rava’s and Abaye’s dilemmas.
topics: 🐑 Rabbi Zeira rereads the mishna: limbs are consecrated, fetuses in the womb are not substituted
🤰 A live four-month-old fetus in a slaughtered sin offering: two baraitot
🚫 Diverse kinds, tereifa, caesarean birth, tumtum and hermaphrodite: “neither sacred nor do they sanctify”
⚖️ Bar Padda and Rabbi Yoḥanan: an unblemished fetus in a blemished mother
🦵 “The leg of this animal is a burnt offering”: does the sanctity spread to all of it?
🩺 Tereifa, carcass or death: Rav Ḥisda, Rava and Rav Sheshet
🕊️ Rava’s dilemmas: a bird, and a limb consecrated for its value
✂️ Shearing and labor with a consecrated limb, skin or fetus

a1.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר: מַקְדִּישִׁין אֵיבָרִין וּמְמִירִין בָּהֶן, אֲבָל לֹא מְמִירִין בָּהֶן, וְעוּבָּרִים שֶׁקָּדְשׁוּ בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן אֵין מְמִירִין בָּהֶן.

a2.he: בְּוַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים, בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן — הוּא דְּלָא עָבְדִין תְּמוּרָה, הָא אַבָּרַאי — עָבְדִי. וְהָא תְּנַן: אֵין הַוְּולָדוֹת עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה! הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא.

a3.he: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵבָרִין מִי קָדְשִׁי? הָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֵית לֵיהּ הָאוֹמֵר ״רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה״ — כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה!

a4.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּדָבָר הָעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה.

a5.he: לֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַחַטָּאת, וּמָצָא בָּהּ בֶּן אַרְבַּע חַי, קָתָנֵי חֲדָא: אֵינָהּ נֶאֱכֶלֶת אֶלָּא לְזִכְרֵי כְהוּנָּה, וְאֵינָהּ נֶאֱכֶלֶת אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים, וְאֵינָהּ נֶאֱכֶלֶת אֶלָּא לְיוֹם אֶחָד.

a6.he: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: נֶאֱכֶלֶת לְכׇל אָדָם, וְנֶאֱכָלִין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם, וְאֵינָן נֶאֱכָלִין בַּעֲזָרָה. מַאי לָאו תַּנָּאֵי הִיא? דְּמָר סָבַר: קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עַל עוּבָּרִין, וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עַל עוּבָּרִין.

a7.he: לָא, הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, דְּמָר סָבַר: וַלְדוֹת קָדָשִׁים בַּהֲוָיָיתָן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים, וּמָר סָבַר: וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים.

a8.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, חַד תַּנָּא הוּא, חֲדָא מֵהָלֵין מַתְנְיָיתָא — בְּמַקְדִּישׁ בְּהֵמָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְעַבְּרָה, וַחֲדָא מִנְּהוֹן — שֶׁהִקְדִּישָׁהּ מְעוּבֶּרֶת.

a9.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כִּלְאַיִם, וּטְרֵפָה, וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, טוּמְטוּם, וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — לֹא קְדוֹשִׁין וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין. וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא קְדוֹשִׁין בִּתְמוּרָה, וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּמוּרָה.

a10.he: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵינָן קְדוֹשִׁין, הֵיאַךְ מַקְדִּישִׁין? אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּמַקְדִּישׁ בְּהֵמָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְרְפָה, בְּמַקְדִּישׁ וָלָד וְיָצָא [דֶּרֶךְ] דּוֹפֶן. אַלְמָא קָדֵישׁ וָלָד!

a11.he: אָמְרִי: בְּתָם בִּמְעֵי תְמִימָה, אֲפִילּוּ בַּר פְּדָא נָמֵי מוֹדֵי דְּקָדֵישׁ. לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּתָם בִּמְעֵי בַּעֲלַת מוּם. בַּר פְּדָא סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאִימֵּיהּ לָא מִקַּדְּשָׁא קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף, הוּא נָמֵי לָא קָדֵישׁ. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: הָנֵי כִּשְׁתֵּי בְהֵמוֹת נִינְהוּ, אִימֵּיהּ הִיא דְּלָא מִיקַּדְּשָׁא, אֲבָל הוּא קָדוֹשׁ.

a12.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, אֲבָל כִּלְאַיִם וְטוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּוַלְדֵי קֳדָשִׁים.

a13.he: וּכְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר: הַוָּלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה. הָלֵין הוּא דְּלָא קָדְשִׁי גּוּפַיְיהוּ, אֲבָל עוּבָּרִין אֲחֵרִים קְדוֹשִׁין!

a14.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תָּם בִּמְעֵי תְּמִימָה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל קָדֵישׁ גּוּפֵיהּ, אֶלָּא כִּי פְּלִיגִי בִּמְעֵי בַּעֲלַת מוּם, דְּבַר פְּדָא סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאִימֵּיהּ נָמֵי לָא קָדֵישׁ גּוּפַהּ — אִיהוּ נָמֵי לָא קָדֵישׁ אֶלָּא לִדְמֵי, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: עוּבָּר לָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִימֵּיהּ לָא קָדְשָׁה לְגוּפַהּ — וָלָד מִיהָא קָדֵישׁ לְגוּפֵיהּ.

a15.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁין, הָאוֹמֵר ״רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ״ כּוּ׳.

b1.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל הָאוֹמֵר ״רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה״ תְּהֵא כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַה׳ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״ — מִמֶּנּוּ לַה׳, וְלֹא כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳.

b2.he: יָכוֹל תֵּצֵא לְחוּלִּין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״. הָא כֵּיצַד? תִּמָּכֵר לְצׇרְכֵי עוֹלוֹת, וְדָמֶיהָ חוּלִּין, חוּץ מִדְּמֵי אֵבֶר שֶׁבָּהּ — דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

b3.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לָאוֹמֵר ״רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה״, שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַה׳״, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״יִהְיֶה קֹדֶשׁ״ — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת כּוּלָּהּ.

b4.he: אָמַר מָר: תִּמָּכֵר לְצׇרְכֵי עוֹלוֹת, וְהָא קָמַיְיתֵי בְּהֵמָה מְחוּסֶּרֶת אֵבֶר? אָמַר רָבָא: בְּאוֹמֵר ״הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ״.

b5.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּדָבָר שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה. רָבָא אָמַר: בְּדָבָר שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ נְבֵילָה. וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: בְּדָבָר שֶׁהִיא מֵתָה.

b6.he: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַב חִסְדָּא לְרָבָא? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ טְרֵפָה חַיָּה. רַב חִסְדָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה אֵינָהּ חַיָּה, וְרָבָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה חַיָּה.

b7.he: וּמַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רָבָא לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: נִיטְּלָה יָרֵךְ וְחָלָל שֶׁלָּהּ — נְבֵילָה. רָבָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.

b8.he: מֵיתִיבִי: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ, וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ. לָאו מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?

b9.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ, מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי. אֶלָּא נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ — לָאו מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? וּתְיוּבְתָּא דְּכוּלְּהוּ!

b10.he: לָא, חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ, שֶׁאַף רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא נֶחְלַק עָלָיו אֶלָּא בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ, אֲבָל בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ.

b11.he: בָּעֵי רָבָא: בָּעוֹף מַהוּ? ״בְּהֵמָה״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהָא לָאו ״בְּהֵמָה״ הִיא, אוֹ דִלְמָא ״קׇרְבָּן״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהַאי נָמֵי ״קׇרְבָּן״ הוּא? תֵּיקוּ.

b12.he: בָּעֵי רָבָא: הִקְדִּישׁ אֵבֶר לְדָמָיו, מַהוּ דְּתֵיחוֹת לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף? מִי אָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּנָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים — נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף, וּמִדְּאַקְדְּשֵׁיהּ לְחַד אֵבֶר — אַקְדְּשַׁיהּ לְכוּלַּהּ, אוֹ דִלְמָא חַד מִגּוֹ אָמַר, תְּרֵי מִגּוֹ לָא אָמַר?

b13.he: תִּפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדִּידֵיהּ, דְּהָאָמַר רָבָא: הִקְדִּישׁ זָכָר לְדָמָיו — קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף!

b14.he: הָתָם — דְּאַקְדְּשֵׁיהּ לְכוּלֵּיהּ, הָכָא — דְּאַקְדְּשֵׁיהּ חַד אֵבֶר, מַאי? תֵּיקוּ.

b15.he: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ [אַבָּיֵי] מֵרָבָא: הִקְדִּישׁ חַד אֵבֶר, מַהוּ בְּגִיזָּה? תִּפְשׁוֹט לָךְ מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא: ״לֹא תָגוֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנְךָ״, אֲבָל אַתָּה גּוֹזֵז בְּשֶׁלְּךָ וְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים.

b16.he: הָתָם, לָא נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשָּׁה כְּלָל; הָכָא, נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשָּׁה. לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: הָתָם, אֵין בְּיָדוֹ לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ; הָכָא, בְּיָדוֹ לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ.

b17.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּיֵי מֵרָבָא: הִקְדִּישׁ עוֹרָהּ, מַהוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה? תָּא שְׁמַע: הָאוֹמֵר ״מָה שֶׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה״ — מוּתֶּרֶת בְּגִיזָּה, וַאֲסוּרָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה, מִפְּנֵי כִּחוּשׁ עוּבָּר שֶׁבָּהּ.

b18.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי קָתָנֵי אֲסוּרָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה — מִדְּרַבָּנַן. אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ בְּגִיזָּה נָמֵי תִּיתְּסַר! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲבוֹדָה דְּמַיכְחֲשָׁא — גָּזְרִי בַּהּ רַבָּנַן, גִּיזָּה — לָא גָּזְרִי בַּהּ רַבָּנַן.

b19.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּיֵי מֵרַב יוֹסֵף: הִיא שְׁלָמִים וּוְלָדָהּ חוּלִּין, וּשְׁחָטָהּ בִּפְנִים, מַהוּ? לְמַאן דְּאָמַר וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים בַּהֲוָיָיתָן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁין, מִי הָוֵי חוּלִּין בַּעֲזָרָה אוֹ לָא?

messages.text: Continued from 10b: bar Padda says fetuses cannot be consecrated; Rabbi Yoḥanan says they can. Rabbi Yirmeya has been raising objections to bar Padda before Rabbi Zeira, most recently from a later mishna (16b): “One consecrates limbs and fetuses, but one does not substitute for them.” Rabbi Zeira said it speaks of offspring of sacrificial animals, and Rabbi Yirmeya asked: then what does “one consecrates” mean, if they are already consecrated?

One consecrates certain animal’s limbs, and the sanctity extends to the entire animal. And therefore, one substitutes these animals despite the fact that he initially consecrated only the limbs. But one does not substitute the limbs alone of non-sacred animals for consecrated animals or their limbs, since sanctity cannot be transferred to a limb through substitution.
messages.lead: Rabbi Zeira answered that this is what the mishna is saying:

notes.dh: הכי קאמר מקדישין איברין וממירין בהן כו'
notes.he: כלומר מקדישין אבר אחד וממירין אחרי כן באותה בהמה ואשמעינן האי וממירין בהן דהאי דקאמר מקדישין אברין לאו למקדיש אבר לחודיה אלא למיפשט קדושה בכולה בהמה דאי אאבר לחודיה לא מצי למימר וממירין בהן דהא אפילו רבי יוסי דאמר ממירין אברין בשלמים מודה דאין ממירין שלימין בהן וכל שכן אברין באברין ודקתני סיפא דהך ברייתא בפ' ב' אבל לא ממירין אשמעינן דאין ממירין בשלימים דאם אמר אבר בהמה זו תמורה לא אקדשיה והיינו חומר בתחילת הקדש מבתמורה דתחילת הקדש כי אקדיש חד אבר פשט בכולה ובתמורה כי אמר אבר זה תמורה תחת שלימה זו לא קדשה:
notes.en: This is what it is saying: One consecrates limbs and one substitutes for them, etc.: That is, one consecrates one limb, and afterward one substitutes [another animal] for that animal. And this “and one substitutes for them” teaches us that when it says “one consecrates limbs,” it does not mean one who consecrates a limb by itself, but that the sanctity spreads through the whole animal. For if it referred to the limb alone, it could not say “and one substitutes for them,” since even Rabbi Yosei, who says one substitutes limbs for whole peace offerings, concedes that one does not substitute whole animals for them, and all the more so limbs for limbs. And what the latter clause of this teaching in the second chapter [16b–17a] teaches, “but one does not substitute,” teaches us that one does not substitute [limbs] for whole animals: if he said, “The limb of this animal is a substitute,” he has not consecrated it. And this is the stringency of initial consecration over substitution: in initial consecration, when he consecrates one limb, [the sanctity] spreads through all of it; but in substitution, when he says, “This limb is a substitute in place of this whole animal,” it is not consecrated.

notes.he: כך גירסת רש"י ור"ל אם פשטה קדושה בכל הבהמה ע"י קדושת הבהמה ממירין בכל הבהמה אבל אמר אבר זה של חולין תהא תמורה לא אמר כלום ונראה דמשום הכי דחיק רש"י לגרוס וממירין משום דפריך עלה בסמוך אברים מי קדישי דאי לא גרס וממירין היכא אשכחנא דאמר אברין קדשי אלא מדקאמר אברין ממירין ועל כרחין היינו כשהקדיש האבר ופשטה קדושה בכל הבהמה ולא נהירא לגרוס וממירין חדא דאינו ברוב הספרים ועוד דבמתניתין גבי חמור בתחילת הקדש מבתמורה תני דאי גרס וממירין אין זה חומר בתחילת הקדש מבתמורה ולכך נראה דלא גרס ליה והא דפריך עלה בסמוך אברים מי קדשי משום דקתני מקדישין עוברין ואברים ובודאי אבר לחודיה לא הקדישו אי לא דפשטה קדושה בכל הבהמה:
notes.en: This is what it is saying: One consecrates limbs and one substitutes: This is Rashi’s reading, and it means: if the sanctity spread through the whole animal by means of the sanctity of [the limb], one substitutes for the whole animal; but if he said, “This limb of a non-sacred animal shall be a substitute,” he has said nothing. And it seems that this is why Rashi was pressed to read “and one substitutes”: because shortly after, [the Gemara] asks on it, “Are limbs consecrated?” For if he did not read “and one substitutes,” where do we find that it says limbs are consecrated? Rather, from the fact that it says one substitutes [for] limbs, it is necessarily where he consecrated the limb and the sanctity spread through the whole animal. But it does not seem correct to read “and one substitutes”: first, because it is not in most books; and furthermore, because in the mishna it is taught among the things more stringent in initial consecration than in substitution, and if one reads “and one substitutes,” this is not a stringency of initial consecration over substitution. Therefore it seems that one does not read it. And as for what [the Gemara] asks on it shortly after, “Are limbs consecrated?”, that is because it teaches “one consecrates fetuses and limbs,” and certainly he could not consecrate a limb alone unless the sanctity spread through the whole animal.

notes.he: תני הכי מקדישין אברין וממירין:
notes.en: It teaches thus: One consecrates limbs and one substitutes for them.

messages.text: And as for fetuses that were consecrated in their mother’s womb through consecration of the mother, one does not substitute for them as long as they are in their mother’s womb. In other words, the clause of this mishna that refers to consecration is not referring to fetuses at all.

notes.he: כגון ולד קדשים אע"פ שהן קדושין אין ממירין בהמה בהן כל זמן שהן במעי אמן והא לאו משום חומר בקדשים מבתמורה קתני אלא משום דתנא וממירין בהן בבהמה שקדשה ע"י אבר תני בעוברין אין ממירין בהן ור' יהודה היא [דאמר] ולד עושה תמורה דאי רבנן אבראי נמי לא עביד תמורה:
notes.en: And fetuses that were consecrated in their mother’s womb: For example, offspring of sacrificial animals. Even though they are consecrated, one does not substitute an animal for them as long as they are in their mother’s womb. And this is not taught as a stringency of sacrificial animals over substitution; rather, since the tanna taught “and one substitutes for them” with regard to an animal consecrated through a limb, he taught with regard to fetuses that one does not substitute for them. And it is Rabbi Yehuda, [who says that] the offspring effects substitution; for if it were the Rabbis, [the offspring] does not effect substitution even outside [the womb].

notes.he: כגון שהקדישן ואח"כ נתעברו אין ממירין בהן ולעולם הא נמי בוולדי קדשים מיירי [אבל בעוברין דעלמא ליכא למשמע [מיניה] אכתי דקדש:
notes.en: And fetuses that were consecrated in their mother’s womb: For example, where he consecrated them [i.e., the mothers] and afterward they became pregnant; one does not substitute for them. And in fact this too deals with offspring of sacrificial animals, [but with regard to ordinary fetuses one cannot yet infer from it that they are consecrated].

messages.text: If the mishna is referring to the offspring of sacrificial animals, and it is teaching that it is only when they are in their mother’s womb that one may not render a substitute for them, one can infer that once they are outside their mother’s womb, one can render a substitute for them. But didn’t we learn in the next mishna that the offspring born of a consecrated animal do not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for them a substitute?
messages.quote: fetuses that were consecrated in their mother’s womb

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this mishna? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who disagrees and maintains that one can substitute for the offspring.

If the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, one encounters a difficulty. According to Rabbi Yehuda, are limbs consecrated in this manner, in that the sanctity extends to the whole animal? But Rabbi Yehuda does not accept that if one says: The hind leg of this animal is a burnt offering, the entire animal is a burnt offering.
messages.quote: in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda

notes.he: אימא רישא מקדישין אברין וממירין בהן והיכי ממירין בהן והא לית ליה לר' יהודה האומר רגלה של זו עולה כולה עולה והכי נמי לענין תמורה:
notes.en: If it is Rabbi Yehuda: Say the first clause: “One consecrates limbs and one substitutes for them.” But how can one substitute for them? Rabbi Yehuda does not hold that one who says, “The leg of this animal is a burnt offering,” makes all of it a burnt offering, and so too with regard to substitution.

messages.text: What are we dealing with here? We are dealing with an item whose removal renders it a tereifa, i.e., will cause it to die within twelve months. Rabbi Yehuda’s ruling that the consecration of a limb does not extend to the entire animal applies only to limbs whose removal would not render the animal a tereifa. He concedes that the consecration of limbs which would render an animal tereifa were they removed does extend to the whole animal. In sum, bar Padda’s opinion that fetuses cannot be consecrated has not been refuted.

notes.he: ר' זירא הא מודי ר' יהודה דאי הקדיש אבר שהנשמה תלויה בו דקדשה כולה ובההוא אבר קאמר מקדישין איברין וממירין בהן ולעולם בוולדי קדשים קא מיירי]:
notes.en: He said to him: Rabbi Zeira [said]: But Rabbi Yehuda concedes that if he consecrated a limb upon which life depends, all of it is consecrated, and it is with regard to that limb that it says “one consecrates limbs and one substitutes for them.” And in fact it deals with offspring of sacrificial animals.

notes.dh: ל"א אבל לא ממירין קתני מיהת מקדישין עוברין
notes.he: א"ל כגון דאקדשינהו לדמיהו דכותה [גבי אבר דאקדיש איברין לדמיהו] וטעמא משו' דאקדשינהו לדמיהו אין ממירין הא אקדשינהו לגופיהן קדשי למעבד תמורה הא אמר ר' יהודה אברין לא קדשי למיהוי כולה תמורה וליכא לאוקומה כר' יהודה א"ל כי תנן מקדישין [עוברין בוולדי קדשים קתני אי בוולדי קדשים כו'] כדתרצינן לעיל בלישנא קמא:
notes.en: Another version: “But one does not substitute”: In any event it teaches “one consecrates fetuses.” He said to him: For example, where he consecrated them for their value, and likewise [with regard to limbs, where he consecrated the limbs for their value]. And the reason one does not substitute is that he consecrated them for their value; but had he consecrated them inherently, they would be consecrated so as to effect substitution. But Rabbi Yehuda said that limbs are not consecrated so that the whole animal becomes a substitute, so one cannot establish [the mishna] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda. He said to him: When we learned “one consecrates [fetuses,” it is teaching about offspring of sacrificial animals. “If offspring of sacrificial animals,” etc.], as we answered above in the first version.

messages.text: Let us say that the dispute between bar Padda and Rabbi Yoḥanan is parallel to a dispute between tanna’im, as we learned: If one slaughtered a pregnant animal that was consecrated as a sin offering, and he found inside it a female fetus four months old, which is alive, despite the fact that the mother usually carries its young for five months,

notes.he: כגון שעירה דאילו כשבה אי אפשר לילד תוך שנתה כדאיתא בבכורות (דף יט:):
notes.en: One who slaughters the sin offering: For example, a female goat; for a ewe cannot give birth within its first year, as stated in Bekhorot (19b).

notes.he: דאילו בן ה' בבהמה דקה אינה ניתרת לרבנן בשחיטת אמו פרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עד.):
notes.en: And he found in it a live four-month-old: For a five-month-old [fetus] in a small animal is not permitted by the slaughter of its mother according to the Rabbis, [as stated in] the chapter Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 74a).

notes.he: בבהמה דקה מיירי דמיעברה לה' חדשים:
notes.en: [And he found in it] a live four-month-old: It is dealing with a small animal, which is pregnant for five months.

messages.text: This animal is treated as a sin offering, and therefore it is eaten only by the males of the priesthood, and it is eaten only within the hangings, i.e., within the Temple courtyard, and it is eaten only for one day and night.

notes.he: כדין חטאת. קא סלקא דעתך דבמפריש בהמה מעוברת עסקינן דאי במפריש ריקנית ונתעברה דכולי עלמא הואיל ומכח אימיה הוא דקדיש חולין הוא דוולדי קדשים בהווייתן הן קדושים כשהן נולדין ולא במעי אמן:
notes.en: Only by the males of the priesthood: As is the law of a sin offering. It enters our mind [at this stage] that we are dealing with one who designates a pregnant animal. For if it were one who designates an empty animal and it became pregnant, everyone would agree that since [the fetus] is consecrated by the power of its mother, it is non-sacred, as offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified at their coming into being, when they are born, and not in their mother’s womb.

messages.text: It is treated as a non-sacred animal, which means it is eaten by any person, not only priests, and such animals may be eaten anywhere outside the Temple courtyard, but they may not be eaten in the Temple courtyard.

What, is it not correct that the dispute between bar Padda and Rabbi Yoḥanan is a dispute between tanna’im, as one Sage, the tanna of the first baraita, holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, that fetuses are imbued with sanctity, and one Sage, the tanna of the second baraita, holds that fetuses are not imbued with sanctity, as maintained by bar Padda?

notes.he: דלתנא קמא קדושה חלה על האברין מכח עצמן כשהיא מעוברת בשעת הקדש קדיש לאלתר דלא כוולדי קדשים הוא ולתנא בתרא אין קדושה חלה עליו אלא מכח אמו וכשאר ולדי קדשים הוא דבהווייתן הוא דקדישי. ולהכי נקט חי רבותא קא משמע לן דלא אמרי' הואיל וחי הוא הווייתו חשיב ליה ואפילו לתנא בתרא ליקדש מכח אמו כשאר ולדי קדשים קא משמע לן דהואיל ולא כלו חדשיו לאו הווייתו הוא:
notes.en: What, is it not a dispute of tanna’im: For according to the first tanna, sanctity takes effect on the limbs [i.e., on the fetus] by their own power: when it was pregnant at the time of consecration, [the fetus] is consecrated immediately, and it is not like the [ordinary] offspring of sacrificial animals. And according to the latter tanna, sanctity takes effect on it only through the power of its mother, and it is like other offspring of sacrificial animals, which are sanctified at their coming into being. And that is why it specified “alive”: it is a novelty. It teaches us that we do not say: since it is alive, this counts as its coming into being, so that even according to the latter tanna it should be consecrated through the power of its mother like other offspring of sacrificial animals. It teaches us that since its months were not complete, this is not its coming into being.

messages.text: No, the tanna’im of both baraitot agree that sanctity can apply to fetuses if the animal was consecrated while pregnant. Rather, the baraitot are dealing with an animal that was consecrated and then became pregnant, and these tanna’im disagree about this, as one Sage, in the second baraita, holds that with regard to the offspring of sacrificial animals, only when they come into being, at the time of their birth, are they sanctified. Since this fetus was never born, it is not sacred.

notes.he: במפריש בהמה מעוברת לא איירי הכא כלל אלא בבהמת קדשים שנתעברה ובהא פליגי תנא קמא סבר ולדות קדשים בהוייתן הן קדושין כשהן נולדין הן קדושין ולא במעי אמן:
notes.en: No: [The baraitot] are not dealing at all with one who designates a pregnant animal, but with a sacrificial animal that became pregnant. And this is what they disagree about: the first tanna holds that offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified at their coming into being, when they are born, and not in their mother’s womb. [Rashi’s “first tanna” is the first view stated in the Gemara’s answer; the Davidson English assigns this view to the second baraita.]

notes.he: לישנא דקרא נקט דאיתרבו ולדות מיניה דכתיב (דברים י״ב:כ״ו) רק קדשיך אשר יהיו לך וגו' ואמר מר אשר יהיו לך אלו הוולדות בפרק שני דבכורות (דף יד:):
notes.en: At their coming into being [bahavayatan]: It uses the language of the verse from which offspring are included, as it is written: “Only your sacred things which you have [asher yihyu lekha]” (Deuteronomy 12:26), and the Master said: “Which you have”: these are the offspring, in the second chapter of Bekhorot (14b).

notes.he: בשעה שיצאו לאויר העולם ובתראה דנתעברה ובסוף הקדישה דלא קדיש וולד דלא אקדיש אלא אם לחודה:
notes.en: At their coming into being they are sacred: At the time they emerge into the air of the world. And in the latter [baraita], where he consecrated [the animal] and in the end it became pregnant, the offspring is not consecrated, since only the mother alone was consecrated, etc. [The printed text, which an editor’s note corrects to the reading above, has instead: where it became pregnant and in the end he consecrated it, the offspring is not consecrated, since he consecrated only the mother alone.]

messages.text: And one Sage, in the first baraita, holds that the offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified already in their mother’s womb, and therefore all the halakhot of a sin offering apply to the fetus immediately.

And if you wish, say instead that there is no contradiction between these two baraitot at all, and it is one tanna who taught both of them, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan that fetuses are imbued with sanctity.

notes.he: הנך תרתי מתנייתא ודכולי עלמא קדושה חלה על העוברין לאלתר כר' יוחנן והך דקתני דלא קדיש עובר במקדיש בהמה ואח"כ נתעברה דוולדות קדשים בהווייתן הן קדושין והאי דקתני דקדיש ולד לאלתר ולא הוי כשאר ולדי קדשים דעובר לאו ירך אמו כשהקדישה מעוברת:
notes.en: And if you wish, say it is one tanna: [Who taught] these two baraitot, and everyone agrees that sanctity takes effect on fetuses immediately, in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan. And the one that teaches that the fetus is not consecrated is where one consecrates an animal and afterward it became pregnant, since offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified at their coming into being. And the one that teaches that the offspring is consecrated immediately, and is not like other offspring of sacrificial animals, [is where] he consecrated [the mother] when pregnant, since a fetus is not the thigh of its mother.

messages.text: And the second one of these baraitot is referring to a case where one consecrates an animal as a sin offering and it became pregnant only afterward. Since the fetus did not exist at the moment of consecration, it is not sacred. And the first one of the baraitot is referring to a case where he consecrated the animal when it was already pregnant, and therefore its fetus is imbued with its sanctity.

An animal crossbred from diverse kinds, and a tereifa, and an animal born by caesarean section, and an animal whose sexual organs are indeterminate [tumtum], and an animal that is a hermaphrodite [ve’androginos] are neither sacred nor do they sanctify another animal.

These animals are not sacred as a substitute, i.e., if one of these was non-sacred it cannot be consecrated as a substitute for a sacred animal. And they do not sanctify another animal to render it a substitute; that is, if one of these animals was sacred, no non-sacred animal can be consecrated as a substitute for them.

notes.he: שאם הן חולין והמירן בבהמת קדשים אינם נתפסין ואפילו תמורה שחלה על בעלי מומין קבועין אינה חלה עליהן וכל שכן אם הקדישם ממש אינן קדושין:
notes.en: They are not sacred as a substitute: That if they are non-sacred and he exchanged them for a sacrificial animal, they are not seized [by sanctity]. And even substitution, which takes effect on animals with permanent blemishes, does not take effect on them; and all the more so if he actually consecrated them, they are not consecrated.

notes.he: אחר לעשותו תמורה אם הן קדושין והמיר בהמת חולין בהן. ורבי מאיר מפרש היכי משכחת לה דליהוי קדושין מאחר שהן אינן קדושין בשום קדושת הגוף מהיכן יהו הן מקדישין ועושין תמורה והא עץ בעלמא נינהו:
notes.en: And they do not sanctify: Another animal to make it a substitute, if they are consecrated and he exchanged a non-sacred animal for them. And Rabbi Meir explains how it can be found that they are consecrated: since they are not consecrated with any inherent sanctity, from where would they sanctify and effect substitution? They are mere wood!

notes.he: [אין קדשין להיות תמורת קדשים ואין מקדישין לעשות תמורה שאם הקדשים הן כלאים וטרפה לא אלימי דלא קדישי למיתפס בהמת חולין בתמורתן]:
notes.en: [They are not sacred to become a substitute for sacrificial animals, and they do not sanctify to effect substitution: for if the sacrificial animals are diverse kinds or a tereifa, they are not strong enough to be consecrated so as to seize a non-sacred animal as their substitute.]

messages.text: Why is it necessary for Rabbi Eliezer to state that one cannot substitute for these animals? After all, since he has already said that they are not sanctified, how could they sanctify another animal exchanged for them?

notes.he: אמר ר' קאי אדר' אלעזר:
notes.en: It is taught: “Rabbi … said”: This refers back to [the statement of] Rabbi Elazar. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s heading gives only “Rabbi,” where the daf has Rabbi Meir, and his text names Rabbi Elazar where the daf has Rabbi Eliezer.]

messages.text: You find that these animals can be sacred, but only in specific situations, for example, where one consecrated an animal and subsequently it became a tereifa, or where one consecrated an animal’s offspring and it was then born by caesarean section.

notes.he: שיהו הן קדושים דלאיצטריך למיתני לא מקדישין אלא במקדיש בהמה ואח"כ נטרפה זו והאי קדושה היא דקדם הקדשה את מומה:
notes.en: You find only: [A case] where they are sacred, so that it was necessary to teach “they do not sanctify,” where one consecrates an animal and afterward it became a tereifa. And this is a sanctity that preceded its blemish.

notes.he: דאיצטריך למימר ולא מקדישין אלא במקדיש בהמה ואח"כ נטרפה [דמעיקרא קדשה כי הויא שלימה והשתא כי נטרפה לא מקדשה לעשות תמורה]:
notes.en: [Rather,] you find: That it was necessary to say “and they do not sanctify” only where one consecrates an animal and afterward it became a tereifa, [for initially it was consecrated when it was whole, and now that it has become a tereifa it does not sanctify to effect substitution].

notes.he: במעי אמו דחיילה עליה קדושה מיד והדר יצא דרך דופן:
notes.en: Where one consecrates an offspring: In its mother’s womb, so that sanctity takes effect on it immediately, and afterward it emerged by caesarean section.

notes.he: במעי אמו ואח"כ יצא דרך דופן [לא מקדיש לאיתפוסי תמורה] אבל טרפה [מעקרו] קודם הקדש ויוצא דופן (מאחר) [לאחר] שנולד לא קדשי גבי קדשים. והאי לאחר שהקדיש יצא דרך דופן [והאי ואח"כ יצא דרך דופן כגון שנגממו או נעקרו כותלי בית הרחם אלמא קדיש וולד במעי אמו ותיובתא לבר פדא:
notes.en: And likewise where one consecrates an offspring: In its mother’s womb, and afterward it emerged by caesarean section, [it does not sanctify so as to seize a substitute]. But a tereifa [from the outset], before consecration, and one born by caesarean section, after it was born, are not consecrated as sacrificial animals. And this one emerged by caesarean section after he consecrated it. [And this “and afterward it emerged by caesarean section” is, for example, where the walls of the womb were cut or torn away. Evidently the offspring is consecrated in its mother’s womb, and this is a refutation of bar Padda.]

notes.he: הני איצטריך למימר דאין מקדישין. וסיפא דמילתא מפרש בפרק יש בקרבנות (לקמן תמורה דף יז.):
notes.en: These needed to be stated: That they do not sanctify. And the conclusion of the matter is explained in the chapter Yesh BaKorbanot (below, Temurah 17a).

messages.text: One can infer from Rabbi Meir’s statement that evidently an offspring can be sanctified while in the womb, contrary to the opinion of bar Padda.
messages.quote: where one consecrated an animal’s offspring and it was then born by caesarean section

messages.text: In the case of an unblemished animal in the womb of an unblemished mother, even bar Padda concedes that it can be consecrated. Bar Padda and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree only with regard to an unblemished animal in the womb of a blemished mother.

notes.he: אמרי בעובר תם במעי תמימה אפי' בר פדא מודי לר' יוחנן דקדיש דומיא דהאי מקדיש וולד ואח"כ יצא דרך דופן] דהיינו תם במעי תמימה כל זמן שהוא במעיה לא נחלקו כו':
notes.en: They say: With an unblemished fetus in the womb of an unblemished mother, even bar Padda concedes to Rabbi Yoḥanan that it is consecrated, similar to this case of one who consecrates an offspring and afterward it emerged by caesarean section], which is an unblemished one in the womb of an unblemished mother, as long as it is in her womb. They disagreed only, etc.

messages.text: Bar Padda maintains that since its mother cannot be consecrated with inherent sanctity, its offspring is not consecrated either. And Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains: These are considered as two separate animals; it is its mother alone that is not consecrated, but the fetus itself is consecrated.

But with regard to an animal born of diverse kinds, and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite, you find that they can be consecrated only when they are offspring of sacrificial animals, i.e., a consecrated animal impregnated by an animal of a different species, or whose fetus was a tumtum or a hermaphrodite.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites another version of the above discussion, which cites the continuation of Rabbi Meir’s statement:

notes.dh: כלאים וטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אי אתה מוצא אלא בולדי קדשים
notes.he: שנתעברה מהן בהמת קדשים לאחר הקדשה אלמא קדיש עובר מדקתני במקדיש עובר ויוצא דרך דופן דהאי הוא דלא קדיש לגופיה למעבד תמורה הא לא יצא דרך דופן קדיש בקדושה קמייתא קדושת הגוף ועביד תמורה וליכא לתרוצי קדושת דמים דאי קדושת דמים לא הוה עביד תמורה אפילו יצא דרך רחם:
notes.en: Diverse kinds, a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, you find only with offspring of sacrificial animals: That a sacrificial animal became pregnant with them after its consecration. Evidently a fetus is consecrated, since it teaches [the case of] one who consecrates a fetus and it emerges by caesarean section: it is this one that is not consecrated inherently so as to effect substitution, but if it did not emerge by caesarean section, it is consecrated with the first sanctity, inherent sanctity, and effects substitution. And one cannot answer [that it refers to] sanctity of value, for if it were sanctity of value it would not effect substitution even if it emerged by way of the womb.

notes.dh: ל"א אבל טומטום [וכלאים ואנדרוגינוס אי אתה מוצא כו']
notes.he: כלומר הני תרי טרפה ויוצא דופן מצית מוקמת לה אפי' בחולין כדאמרן אבל כלאים וטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אי אתה מוצא בקדשים דקדישי אלא בוולדי קדשים בעוברי קדשים דהני לא הוו להו שעת הכושר מעולם דמשעת יצירת נפסלו [נעשו כלאים וטומטום ואנדרוגינוס] (אלא) ולא קדשו אלא אגב אימיהו להכי קאמר אי אתה מוצא אלא בוולדות קדשים וכר' יהודה דאמר הולד עושה תמורה:
notes.en: Another version: But a tumtum [and diverse kinds and a hermaphrodite, you find only, etc.]: That is, these two, a tereifa and one born by caesarean section, you can establish even [where they were] non-sacred, as we said. But diverse kinds, a tumtum and a hermaphrodite you do not find among sacrificial animals that are consecrated, except with offspring of sacrificial animals, with fetuses of sacrificial animals, for these never had a time of fitness: from the time of their formation they were disqualified [they were formed as diverse kinds, tumtum or hermaphrodite], and they were consecrated only by virtue of their mothers. That is why it says “you find only with offspring of sacrificial animals,” and it is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says the offspring effects substitution.

messages.text: And Rabbi Eliezer holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who would say that the offspring of a consecrated animal renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute. These offspring are exceptions, as they are disqualified for the altar.

It is only for these disqualified offspring that one cannot substitute, as they cannot have inherent sanctity, but other offspring that are fit for the altar, and likewise other fetuses, can be consecrated, contrary to the opinion of bar Padda.

notes.he: אלא אגב אימיהו דלא קדישי אלא לדמים משום דבעלי מומין נינהו אבל עוברין אחריני דלאו עוברין אחרינין נינהו קדשי גופייהו אפי' במעי אימן חולין וקשיא לבר פדא אמר אביי בתם במעי תמימין כו' כדלעיל:
notes.en: It is these that are not consecrated inherently: But only by virtue of their mothers, for they are consecrated only for their value, since they are blemished. But other fetuses [the text repeats itself here] are consecrated inherently, even in the womb of their non-sacred mothers. And this is difficult for bar Padda. Abaye said: With an unblemished one in the womb of an unblemished mother, etc., as above.

messages.text: In the case of an unblemished animal in the womb of an unblemished mother, everyone agrees that the fetus can have inherent sanctity. Rather, when bar Padda and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree, it is with regard to an unblemished animal in the womb of a blemished mother.

As bar Padda maintains: Since even its mother cannot have inherent sanctity, the offspring too can be consecrated only for its value. And Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains: A fetus is considered not the thigh of its mother but a separate entity, and therefore even though its mother’s sanctity is not inherent, the sanctity of its offspring can still be inherent.
But isn’t it so with regard to sacrificial animals, that if one says: The hind leg of this animal is a burnt offering, the entire animal is a burnt offering? The same should apply to substitution.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that according to the Rabbis, one cannot substitute non-sacred limbs for whole consecrated animals, but Rabbi Yosei said that one can substitute in this manner. He claims:

messages.text: One might have thought that if one says: The leg of this animal is a burnt offering, the sanctity should extend to the whole animal and all of the animal will be a burnt offering. Therefore, the verse states: “And if it is an animal of those that they bring as an offering to the Lord, anything of it that one gives to the Lord, it shall be sacred”. The verse indicates that the part of it that one gives will be sacred unto the Lord, and not all of the animal will be sacred unto the Lord.

verse.he: וְאִם־בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַיהֹוָה יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any animal that may be brought as an offering to GOD, any such that may be given to GOD shall be holy.

messages.text: If so, one might have thought that the consecrated limb may be redeemed and thereby transferred to non-sacred status. Therefore the verse states: “Shall be sacred,” teaching that the limb remains consecrated. How is this possible, i.e., what should one do with the animal? The animal should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings to an individual who will sacrifice the entire animal as a burnt offering, and the payment received for the animal will be non-sacred, except for the payment received in exchange for the limb of the animal that was consecrated.

notes.he: ההוא אבר וכיון דההוא אבר הוי קדוש תו לא מצי למשחט ההיא בהמה לשם חולין אלא תמכר כולה חוץ מדמי אותו אבר שבה דדמי אותו אבר לא יטול שהרי הקדישו ואינו יכול למוכרו:
notes.en: Shall be sacred: That limb. And since that limb is sacred, he can no longer slaughter that animal as non-sacred; rather, all of it shall be sold except for the value of that limb in it. For he does not take the value of that limb, since he consecrated it and cannot sell it.

messages.text: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: הכי גרסי' דברי רבי מאיר ור' יהודה:
notes.en: This is how we read: The statement of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: From where is it derived in the case of one who says: The leg of this animal is a burnt offering, that all of it becomes a burnt offering? Since it is stated: “All that any man give of such to the Lord shall be sacred”, one might have thought that individual limbs can be consecrated. When it says: “Shall be sacred,” this phrase serves to include all of the animal, indicating that it all becomes sacred.
messages.lead: But Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:

verse.he: וְאִם־בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַיהֹוָה יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any animal that may be brought as an offering to GOD, any such that may be given to GOD shall be holy.

messages.text: The animal should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings. But it is as though the purchaser is bringing an animal that lacks that limb that was consecrated by the previous owner, as his share in the offering consists only of the balance of the animal.
messages.quote: The animal should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings

notes.he: דמעיקרא איקדש מינה אבר:
notes.en: [But he is bringing] an animal lacking a limb: Since initially a limb of it was consecrated.

notes.he: שהרי אותו האבר אינו שלו אלא לחובת המוכר הוא קרב נמצא שהלוקח זה לא הקריב עולה שלימה והוא נדר להקריב כל הבהמה לחובתו:
notes.en: Lacking a limb: For that limb is not his; rather, it is sacrificed for the obligation of the seller. It emerges that this purchaser did not sacrifice a whole burnt offering, though he vowed to sacrifice the whole animal for his obligation.

messages.text: The baraita does not mean that the animal should be sold to anyone obligated to bring a burnt offering, but specifically to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering with all the limbs upon which its life depends. Since the consecrated limb is not one of these, it does not detract from the purchaser’s vow.

notes.he: הרי עלי להקריב כל האברין שהבהמה חיה ממנה והרי כן עשה דהמוכר לא הקדיש אלא אבר שאינה חיה ממנו כגון רגל מן הארכובה ולמטה שאם היה מקדיש דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו הוה פשטה קדושה בכולה כדאמר מודה ר' יהודה בדבר שעושה אותה טריפה שאם הקדיש אבר שממנו נטרפת אם היה ניטל פשטה קדושה בכולה אפי' לר' יהודה. לישנא אחרינא ירושלמי והא מייתי בהמה דמקדיש גופה כי ליתיה כולה לדידיה כלומר האי לוקח הא מייתי בהמה שאין הגוף שלו ומשני כגון דאמר כזוזא מן הדא בהמה לעולה כלומר שוה זוז מבהמה זו לעולה והרי קנה זוז (וזוז) הלכך יצא דהא לא נדר עולה שלימה:
notes.en: Where he says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering with its life: It is incumbent upon me to sacrifice all the limbs from which the animal lives. And he has done so, for the seller consecrated only a limb from which it does not live, for example, the leg from the knee joint downward. For had he consecrated a thing upon which life depends, the sanctity would have spread through all of it, as it says: Rabbi Yehuda concedes with regard to a thing that renders it a tereifa, that if he consecrated a limb whose removal would render it a tereifa, the sanctity spreads through all of it even according to Rabbi Yehuda. Another version, [from the] Jerusalem [Talmud]: “But he is bringing an animal whose body he consecrates when it is not all his”; that is, this purchaser is bringing an animal whose body is not [entirely] his. And it answers: For example, where he said, “A zuz’s worth of this animal for a burnt offering,” that is, a zuz’s worth of this animal as a burnt offering, and he has acquired a zuz’s worth. Therefore he has fulfilled [his vow], for he did not vow a whole burnt offering.

notes.he: זה הקונה אותה אומר בשעת נדרו הרי עלי עולה]:
notes.en: [Ravina said: Where he says: This purchaser says at the time of his vow: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering.] [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads Ravina here, where the daf has Rava.]

notes.he: בחייה כלומר (באומר זה הקונה בשעת נדרו) הרי עלי (בהמה) להביא עולה שיכולה לחיות ואפי' היתה מחוסרת אותו [אבר] שהוקדש מקודם היתה יכולה לחיות ומה שנדר הביא. ל"א והא קא מייתי בהמה כו'. [אלא אמר רבא כגון דאמר בשעת נדרו הרי עלי] בזוזא (כלומר לא אמר בשעת נדרו אלא בשוה זוז) מן [הדא] בהמה לעולה [דלא קבל עליו אלא בשוה זוז ממנה לעולה] דהשתא [חוץ] מאותו אבר המוקדש [עדיין יש בה] שוה כמה זוזים ומה (שנדר) [ששוה יותר] יכול להביא [מודה ר' יהודה]:
notes.en: With its life: That is, (where this purchaser says at the time of his vow:) It is incumbent upon me (an animal) to bring a burnt offering that can live; and even though it was lacking that [limb] that was consecrated earlier, it could live, and he has brought what he vowed. Another version: “But he is bringing an animal,” etc. [Rather, Rava said: For example, where he said at the time of his vow: It is incumbent upon me] a zuz’s worth (that is, at the time of his vow he said only a zuz’s worth) of [this] animal as a burnt offering, [for he took upon himself only a zuz’s worth of it as a burnt offering]. Now, [apart] from that consecrated limb, [it is still] worth several zuz, and he can bring [what is worth more]. [The note ends with the words “Rabbi Yehuda concedes,” which head the next passage.]

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir concede with regard to a limb whose removal renders the animal a tereifa. If one consecrated such a limb, the sanctity extends throughout the entire animal.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites a dispute between amora’im:

notes.he: דפשטה קדושה בכולה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda concedes: That the sanctity spreads through all of it.

notes.he: [דאי אקדיש אבר מינה שהנשמה תלויה בו] כגון לב או כבד [דקדשה כולה או] בדבר שעושה טרפה [אם ניטל ממנה אותו אבר כגון] שנחתך רגלה מן הארכובה ולמעלה:
notes.en: With regard to a thing upon which life depends: [For if he consecrated a limb of it upon which life depends,] for example, the heart or the liver, [all of it is consecrated; or] with regard to a thing that renders it a tereifa [if that limb is removed from it, for example,] where its leg was cut off from the knee joint upward.

messages.text: Even in such a case, Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda maintain that the sanctity does not extend throughout the entire animal. Yet, they concede with regard to a limb whose removal renders it an animal carcass, i.e., without which the animal would die so soon that it assumes the status of a carcass.

notes.he:
כגון הירך וחלל שלה אבל בדבר העושה אותה טרפה כמו רגלה מן הארכובה ולמעלה לא מודה וטעמא מפרש לקמיה:
כגון הלב או הוושט:
notes.en: That renders it a carcass: For example, the thigh and its recess. But with regard to a thing that renders it a tereifa, such as its leg from the knee joint upward, he does not concede, and the reason is explained below. [A further gloss follows, apparently on Rav Sheshet’s “that it dies”:] For example, the heart or the gullet.

notes.he: כמאן דאמר טרפה חיה להכי קאמר בדבר שעושה אותה נבילה כגון ניטל הירך וחלל שלה [נבילה]:
notes.en: And Rava holds: In accordance with the one who says a tereifa can survive. That is why he says “with regard to a thing that renders it a carcass,” for example, where the thigh and its recess were removed, [which is a carcass].

messages.text: They conceded only with regard to a limb whose removal would cause it to die immediately.

What difference is there between the opinion of Rav Ḥisda and that of Rava? The difference between them is with regard to the issue of whether a tereifa can survive. Rav Ḥisda holds in accordance with the opinion of the one who said that a tereifa cannot survive but will shortly die. Therefore, Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda concede that if one consecrates a limb whose removal would render an animal a tereifa, the sanctity applies to the whole animal, since it is a vital organ.

notes.he: פלוגתא היא באלו טרפות (חולין דף מב.) הלכך כיון דאינה חיה הרי הקדיש דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו הלכך מודי:
notes.en: In accordance with the one who says a tereifa cannot survive: It is a dispute in the chapter Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 42a). Therefore, since it cannot survive, he has consecrated a thing upon which life depends, and therefore [Rabbi Yehuda] concedes.

messages.text: And Rava holds in accordance with the opinion of the one who says that a tereifa can survive, and consequently the consecration of such a limb does not extend to the entire animal.

notes.he: ואינו דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו:
notes.en: And Rava holds a tereifa can survive: And it is not a thing upon which life depends.

notes.dh: רב חסדא סבר כמאן דאמר טריפה אינה חיה ורבא סבר כמאן דאמר טריפה חיה
notes.he: ובפ"ק דבכורות (דף ג.) נהפכה סוגיא זאת גבי שותפות עובד כוכבים דרב חסדא סבר טריפה חיה וזו מן הסוגיות הפוכות שבהש"ס וכן מצינו בשאר דוכתי גבי פלוגתא דאביי ורבא דידים מוכיחות במסכת נדרים (דף ה:) ובמסכת נזיר (דף סב. ע"ש) ומיהו צריך עיון לפי הא דאמר רבא הכא טריפה חיה דבפרק החולץ (יבמות דף לו) אמר רבא גבי ספק טרפה משהינן לה י"ב חדש:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda holds in accordance with the one who says a tereifa cannot survive, and Rava holds in accordance with the one who says a tereifa can survive: In the first chapter of Bekhorot (3a) this discussion is reversed, with regard to partnership with a gentile, where Rav Ḥisda holds a tereifa can survive; and this is one of the reversed discussions in the Talmud. And so we find in other places with regard to the dispute between Abaye and Rava about “the hands prove,” in tractate Nedarim (5b) and in tractate Nazir (62a; see there). However, this requires examination according to what Rava says here, that a tereifa can survive, for in the chapter HaḤoletz (Yevamot 36a) Rava says with regard to an animal that is possibly a tereifa that we wait with it twelve months.

messages.text: And what difference is there between the opinion of Rava and the opinion of Rav Sheshet? The difference between them is with regard to the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, as Rabbi Elazar said:
If the thigh, i.e., the hind leg of the animal, and its recess were removed, the animal is considered a carcass and imparts ritual impurity even while still alive.

notes.he: אע"פ שהיא עדיין חיה מטמאה כנבלה דכמתה היא ולא כחיה:
notes.en: If the thigh and its recess were removed, it is a carcass: Even though it is still alive, it imparts impurity like a carcass, for it is like a dead animal and not like a living one.

messages.text: Rava holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, and therefore he maintains that according to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda, if one consecrates its thigh and its recess the sanctity extends throughout the animal, as it is a vital limb.

notes.he: הילכך אקדיש ירך וחלל שלה הוי דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו:
notes.en: Rava holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar: Therefore, if he consecrated the thigh and its recess, it is a thing upon which life depends.

messages.text: But Rav Sheshet does not hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, and therefore the sanctity in such a case does not extend to the entire animal.

notes.dh: ורב ששת לית ליה דר' אלעזר
notes.he: בפ"ק דחולין (דף כא.) מפרש היכי דמי חלל שלה כל שרבוצה ונראית חסרה:
notes.en: And Rav Sheshet does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Elazar: In the first chapter of Ḥullin (21a) it explains what “its recess” is: whatever, when [the animal] lies down, appears to be lacking.

notes.dh: רב ששת לא סבר לה כר' אלעזר
notes.he: להכי קאמר בדבר שהיא מתה מיד ולא שתהא מפרכסת [אלמא בתרווייהו פליגי:
notes.en: Rav Sheshet does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Elazar: That is why he says “with regard to a thing [without which] it dies” immediately, and not that it would still be convulsing. [Evidently they disagree about both.]

messages.caption: Which consecrated limb spreads its sanctity to the whole animal, even for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda: Rav Ḥisda, Rava and Rav Sheshet.

messages.text: With regard to the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei, the statement of Rabbi Yehuda, that the sanctity does not extend to the whole animal, appears correct with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life does not depend, and the statement of Rabbi Yosei appears correct with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life depends.

May one not conclude by inference from the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi that Rabbi Yosei disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda even with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life depends, contrary to the statements of the amora’im above?

Granted, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s comment: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears correct with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life does not depend, is not difficult, as one learns by inference only that Rabbi Yehuda disagrees with Rabbi Yosei with regard to such a case. But when he says that the statement of Rabbi Yosei appears correct with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life depends, must one not conclude by inference that Rabbi Yosei disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda with regard to this case as well?
messages.quote: the statement of Rabbi Yosei appears correct with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life depends

messages.text: And this is apparently a conclusive refutation of all the opinions of the amora’im cited above, who maintain that Rabbi Yehuda concedes with regard to vital organs.

notes.he: דרב חסדא ורבה ורב ששת:
notes.en: And a refutation of all of them: Of Rav Ḥisda, Rabba and Rav Sheshet. [Rabbeinu Gershom writes Rabba where the daf has Rava.]

messages.text: No, the baraita citing Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s statement is incomplete, and this is what it is teaching: The statement of Rabbi Yosei appears correct to Rabbi Yehuda in the case of a limb upon which the animal’s life depends, as even Rabbi Yehuda disagreed with Rabbi Yosei only with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life does not depend. But with regard to a limb upon which the animal’s life depends, Rabbi Yehuda concedes to him that the sanctity extends to the entire animal.

notes.dh: הכי קאמר נראין דברי רבי יוסי לר' יהודה
notes.he: דר' יהודה מודה ליה בדבר שהנשמה תלויה בו:
notes.en: This is what it is saying: The statement of Rabbi Yosei appears correct to Rabbi Yehuda: For Rabbi Yehuda concedes to him with regard to a thing upon which life depends.

notes.dh: אלא חסורי מחסרא והכי קתני כו'
notes.he: ולא קשיא להו:
notes.en: Rather, [the baraita] is incomplete and this is what it is teaching, etc. And [the amora’im] are not difficult.

messages.text: With regard to a bird that is fit for sacrifice, what is the halakha according to this opinion? Since this halakha is derived, as stated above, from the verse: “And if it is an animal of those that they bring as an offering to the Lord, anything of it that one gives to the Lord, it shall be sacred”, one can contend that the Merciful One states “animal,” and this bird is not considered an animal. Or perhaps one should stress that the Merciful One states “offering,” and this bird is also considered an offering.
messages.lead: § According to Rabbi Yosei, if one consecrates one limb of an animal the sanctity extends to the entire animal. Rava raises a dilemma:

verse.he: וְאִם־בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַיהֹוָה יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any animal that may be brought as an offering to GOD, any such that may be given to GOD shall be holy.

notes.he: לר' יוסי קא בעי לה הקדיש רגל עוף דתור או בן יונה מי פשטה קדושה בכוליה או לא:
notes.en: With regard to a bird, what is the halakha: He asks according to Rabbi Yosei: If one consecrated the leg of a bird, of a turtledove or a young pigeon, does the sanctity spread through all of it or not?

notes.he: בהאי קרא מכל אשר יתן ממנו כתיב בהמה וקרבן:
notes.en: The Merciful One states “animal”: In this verse, “anything of it that one gives,” both “animal” and “offering” are written.

notes.he: אמר ר' יוסי דאי אקדיש רגל מן העוף הוי נמי כולו קדוש אי לא מי אמרינן קרבן אמר רחמנא ואם בהמה אשר יקריבו ממנה קרבן לה' והאי נמי קרבן הוא]:
notes.en: With regard to a bird, what is the halakha: [According to] Rabbi Yosei, if one consecrated a leg of a bird, is all of it sacred as well or not? Do we say: The Merciful One states “offering” (“And if it is an animal of which they bring an offering to the Lord”), and this too is an offering?

messages.text: The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

According to Rabbi Yosei, if one consecrated a limb with the intention of selling it and purchasing an offering with its payment, what is the halakha as to whether the entire animal is imbued with inherent sanctity? Does one say that since it is imbued with sanctity that inheres in its value, it is likewise imbued with inherent sanctity, and then furthermore, from the fact that he consecrated one limb he has consecrated the entire animal?

notes.dh: הקדיש אבר לדמיו מהו דתיחות קדושת הגוף
notes.he: לכל הבהמה ותיקרב עולה מי אמר לרבי יוסי מדאקדיש חד אבר לדמיו פשטה קדושה לכולה בהמה לדמיה ומיגו דנחתא לה קדושת דמים לכולה בהמה נחתא לה קדושת הגוף הואיל והיא גופא חזיא לעולה למה לי למוכרה ולהביא בדמיה עולה הלכך בעל כרחיה קדשי קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: If one consecrated a limb for its value, what is the halakha as to inherent sanctity descending upon it: Upon the whole animal, so that it is sacrificed as a burnt offering? Do we say according to Rabbi Yosei: since he consecrated one limb for its value, the sanctity spread to the whole animal for its value; and since sanctity of value descended upon the whole animal, inherent sanctity descends upon it, since its body itself is fit for a burnt offering? Why should he need to sell it and bring a burnt offering with its value? Therefore it is necessarily consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: Or perhaps one says a claim using the logic that begins with: Since, only once, but one does not say two claims together using the logic that begins with: Since, i.e., one cannot make both of the suggested expansions simultaneously.

notes.he: חד דהוא לא אקדיש אלא אבר ולדמיו ואנן צריכין לומר מגו דחייל אאבר חייל אכולה בהמה לדמיה ומגו דנחית כולה לדמיה נחית נמי כולה לקדושת הגוף:
notes.en: Two [claims of] “since”: One, that he consecrated only a limb, and for its value, and we need to say: since [the sanctity] takes effect on the limb, it takes effect on the whole animal for its value; and [two,] since all of it descends [into sanctity] for its value, all of it also descends into inherent sanctity.

messages.text: Resolve the dilemma by citing Rava’s own statement. As, didn’t Rava say:
messages.quote: if one consecrated a limb with the intention of selling it and purchasing an offering with its payment

notes.he: דודאי נחתא לה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: Resolve it from his own statement: That certainly inherent sanctity descends upon it.

messages.text: If one consecrated a male ram for its value, since the ram is fit for sacrifice, it is automatically consecrated with inherent sanctity.

notes.he: איל זכר. ולהכי נקט רבא זכר דבעולה איירי רבא ונקבה לא חזיא לעולה וליכא למימר קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: For Rava said: If one consecrated a male: A male ram. And Rava specified a male because Rava is speaking of a burnt offering, and a female is not fit for a burnt offering, so one could not speak of inherent sanctity.

notes.he: להביא בדמיו עולה קדוש קדושת הגוף ואינו יכול למכרו הואיל והוא גופיה חזיא לעולה והוא עצמו יקרב לעולה. והכא נמי הואיל ולרבי יוסי נחתא קדושה לכולה על ידי האבר קדשה נמי לגופה:
notes.en: For its value: To bring a burnt offering with its value. It is consecrated with inherent sanctity, and he cannot sell it, since it itself is fit for a burnt offering, and it itself shall be sacrificed as a burnt offering. And here too, since according to Rabbi Yosei the sanctity descends upon all of it by means of the limb, it is consecrated inherently as well.

notes.he: פשוט מן הא דאמרת הקדיש זכר [דראוי לעולה הקדישו] לדמיו קדוש קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: Resolve it from what you said: If one consecrated a male [fit for a burnt offering, consecrating it] for its value, it is consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: The same reasoning should apply here: Although the limb was consecrated for its value, since the animal is fit for sacrifice, once the entire animal is consecrated for its value it should automatically assume inherent sanctity.

This is not a proof: There, where he initially consecrated all of it, the whole animal assumes inherent sanctity. Here, Rava is referring to a case where he consecrated only one limb at the outset, and one must invoke two separate expansions to apply inherent sanctity to the whole animal. The question stands: What is the halakha? The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

notes.he: וליכא אלא חד מיגו:
notes.en: There, where he consecrated all of it: And there is only one [claim of] “since.”

notes.he: [משום] דאקדשיה כוליה לדמיו ומגו דנחתי קדושת [דמים אכולה] (לכולו לדמיו) נחתא ליה קדושת הגוף [נמי לכולו]:
notes.en: There: [Because] he consecrated all of it for its value, and since sanctity of [value descends upon all of it], inherent sanctity [also] descends upon [all of it].

notes.he: ל"א חד מגו אמרינן [הוא דאמרן תרי מגו מגו דאקדיש חד אבר קדשה כו' ומגו דקדשה לדמיה קדש קדושת הגוף] תרי מגו לא אמרינן:
notes.en: Another version: One [claim of] “since” we say [that is what we said]. Two [claims of] “since” [since he consecrated one limb, all of it is consecrated, etc., and since it is consecrated for its value, it is consecrated with inherent sanctity] we do not say.

messages.text: If one consecrated one limb, what is the halakha with regard to shearing the wool of that limb?
messages.lead: § According to Rabbi Yehuda, if one consecrates a limb, the sanctity does not extend to the entire animal. A Sage posed a dilemma to Rava:

notes.he: בעבודה לא תיבעי לך דאסור דהא מכחיש לה:
notes.en: If one consecrated a limb, what is the halakha with regard to shearing: With regard to labor you need not ask, for it is prohibited, since it weakens [the animal].

messages.text: The printed Aramaic adds “Abaye” in brackets as the one who asked; the Davidson English reads “a Sage.”
You can resolve the dilemma from that which is taught in a baraita:

The verse states: “Nor shear the firstborn of your flock”. This verse indicates that the prohibition against shearing applies only to an animal belonging entirely to you, but you may shear the wool of a firstborn that belongs both to you and to others, i.e., gentiles.

verse.he: כׇּל־הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃
verse.en: You shall consecrate to the ETERNAL your God all male firstlings that are born in your herd and in your flock: you must not work your firstling ox or shear your firstling sheep.

notes.he: עובד כוכבים. אם יש לך בכור בשותפות עם העובד כוכבים מותר לגוזזו הכא נמי הואיל והחולין והקדש שותפין בו מותר:
notes.en: Yours and others’: A gentile. If you have a firstborn in partnership with a gentile, it is permitted to shear it. Here too, since non-sacred and consecrated are partners in it, it is permitted.

messages.text: Here too, since the animal is jointly owned by the Temple and by the one who consecrated it, the prohibition against shearing should not apply at all.

There, a firstborn animal owned partly by a gentile was not imbued with sanctity at all, whereas here it was at least partly imbued with sanctity, and therefore it is possible that the limb is prohibited with respect to shearing.
messages.lead: The Sage responded that this is not a proof:
messages.quote: since the animal is jointly owned by the Temple and by the one who consecrated it

notes.he: גבי בכור לא נחתא ליה שום קדושה ואפי' לחלקו של ישראל דשותפות עובד כוכבים פוטרת מן הבכורה הכא נחתא קדושה להך אבר:
notes.en: There: With regard to the firstborn, no sanctity at all descended upon it, even upon the Jew’s share, for partnership with a gentile exempts [an animal] from firstborn status. Here, sanctity descended upon that limb.

notes.dh: התם לא נחתא ליה קדושת הגוף
notes.he: פירש רש"י דסבר דשותפות העובד כוכבים פוטרת מן הבכורה ובפ"ק דבכורות (דף ג:) קאמר אפי' למ"ד שותפות העובד כוכבים אינו פוטר והא דאמר התם לא נחתא ליה קדושה ר"ל להקריב:
notes.en: There, inherent sanctity did not descend upon it: Rashi explained that [the Gemara] holds that partnership with a gentile exempts from firstborn status. But in the first chapter of Bekhorot (3b) it says [this] even according to the one who says partnership with a gentile does not exempt; and what it says there, “sanctity did not descend upon it,” means [sanctity] to be sacrificed.

notes.dh: הא נמי שלו ושל אחרים [היא] דחד אבר מינה הוא דקדיש ושאר הגוף דדחולין הוא
notes.he: א"ל התם לא נחתא ליה קדושה בכולה דחציה דעובד כוכבים היא וחלק עובד כוכבים לא קדיש הכא דכולה שלו הויא נחתא קדושה בכולה ואסורה כולה בגיזה. הקדיש שה כי לישנא אחרינא:
notes.en: This too is “yours and others’”: For only one limb of it is consecrated and the rest of the body is non-sacred. He said to him: There, sanctity did not descend upon all of it, since half of it belongs to the gentile, and the gentile’s share is not consecrated. Here, where all of it is his, sanctity descends upon all of it, and all of it is prohibited for shearing. [The note ends with the unclear words “He consecrated a lamb, as in another version.”]

messages.text: There, in the case of a firstborn animal owned partly by a gentile, it is not in the Jew’s power to consecrate his share. Therefore, the prohibition against shearing does not apply. But here it is in his power to consecrate one limb, and sanctity applies to it. Therefore, one can claim that the limb should be prohibited with respect to shearing.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites another version of this answer:

notes.he: הואיל ויש לעובד כוכבים שותפות בו:
notes.en: It is not in his power to consecrate it: Since the gentile has a partnership in it.

messages.text: If one consecrated only the skin of an animal, what is the halakha as to whether it may be used for labor?

notes.he: של בהמה מהו בעבודה בגיזה לא תיבעי לך דלא מכחיש ליה לעור אבל עבודה מכחשא ליה לעור:
notes.en: If one consecrated its skin: Of an animal, what is the halakha with regard to labor? With regard to shearing you need not ask, for it does not weaken the skin; but labor weakens the skin.

notes.he: כלומר בגיזה לא קא מיבעיא ליה דודאי אסורה מפני כחש העור כי קא מיבעיא ליה בעבודה:
notes.en: The skin, what is the halakha with regard to labor: That is, he is not asking about shearing, for it is certainly prohibited because of the weakening of the skin; he is asking about labor. [So the text reads; Rashi writes that shearing does not weaken the skin.]

messages.text: Come and hear a baraita:

In the case of one who says: That which is in the womb of this animal is a burnt offering, it is permitted for the mother to be shorn but it is prohibited to use the animal for labor, due to the inevitable weakening of the fetus inside it.

notes.he: והכא נמי איכא כחוש עור:
notes.en: Due to the weakening of the fetus: And here too there is weakening of the skin.

messages.text: The same should apply to an animal whose skin alone was consecrated, as performing labor with the animal would reduce the value of its skin.
When that baraita teaches that it is prohibited to use the mother for labor, this applies by rabbinic law. I was asking whether it is prohibited by Torah law.

notes.he: וכי מיבעיא ליה מדאורייתא ולמילקי עליה:
notes.en: By rabbinic law: And he is asking about Torah law, [whether] one would receive lashes for it.

notes.dh: ת"ש האומר מה שבמעיה של זו עולה מותר בגיזה ואסורה בעבודה
notes.he: מפני כחש עובר. הכא נמי עבודה מכחיש העור ואסור דכשהיא שמינה מוטב העור א"ל מיהא לא תפשוט דכי קתני הכא אסורה בעבודה מדרבנן קתני ולא מדאורייתא ואנא גבי עור בעינא אי אסור מדאורייתא אי הכי אי מדרבנן אפי' בגיזה נמי ליתסר מדרבנן גבי עובר א"ל כו':
notes.en: Come hear: One who says, “That which is in the womb of this animal is a burnt offering,” it is permitted for shearing and prohibited for labor, due to the weakening of the fetus. Here too, labor weakens the skin and is prohibited, for when [the animal] is fat the skin is better. He said to him: You cannot resolve it from here, for when it teaches here “prohibited for labor,” it teaches that it is by rabbinic law and not by Torah law, and I am asking about the skin, whether it is prohibited by Torah law. If so, if it is by rabbinic law, then let even shearing be prohibited by rabbinic law with regard to the fetus. He said to him, etc.

messages.text: If so, that the baraita is referring to rabbinic law, then even shearing it should be prohibited.

With regard to labor, which weakens the animal, the Sages issued a decree rendering it prohibited; with regard to shearing, which does not weaken the animal, the Sages did not issue a decree rendering it prohibited.
messages.quote: even shearing it should be prohibited

messages.text: If one consecrates a pregnant animal as a peace offering but excludes its fetus, and as a result it is sanctified as a peace offering and its offspring is non-sacred, and he slaughtered the pregnant animal inside the Temple courtyard as appropriate for a peace offering, what is the halakha?

notes.he: הקדיש בהמה מעוברת חוץ מעוברה דלדברי הכל אין העובר קדוש:
notes.en: It is a peace offering and its offspring is non-sacred: He consecrated a pregnant animal except for its fetus, so that according to everyone the fetus is not sacred.

notes.dh: היא שלמים וולדה חולין ושחטה בפנים מהו
notes.he: פירוש אם הולד אסור משום חולין בעזרה ונראה דמצי למיפשטיה מההיא דלעיל דהשוחט את החטאת ומצא בה בן ד' חי משמע דלא הוי חולין בעזרה:
notes.en: It is a peace offering and its offspring is non-sacred, and he slaughtered it inside, what is the halakha: That is, whether the offspring is prohibited as a non-sacred animal [slaughtered] in the courtyard. And it seems that he could have resolved it from that [baraita] above, “one who slaughters the sin offering and finds in it a live four-month-old,” which implies that it is not [prohibited as] a non-sacred animal in the courtyard.

messages.text: Or, if one consecrates an animal and it subsequently becomes pregnant, then according to the one who said that the offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified only when they come into being, i.e., at the time of their birth, are offspring such as this subject to the prohibition against slaughtering non-sacred animals in the Temple courtyard, since they are not yet born? Or are they not subject to the prohibition, since they themselves were not slaughtered?

notes.dh: למאן דאמר וולדות קדשים בהווייתן הן קדושין
notes.he: כלומר אדם שהקדיש בהמה ואחר כך נתעברה ומיבעיא לי אליבא דמאן דאמר וולדות קדשים בהווייתן הן קדושין והשתא מיהא לא קדיש עובר ושחטה לאם בפנים בעזרה מי הוי ולד חולין בעזרה ומחייב דהא לא הקדיש עובר או לא:
notes.en: According to the one who said offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified at their coming into being: That is, a person consecrated an animal and afterward it became pregnant, and I ask according to the one who says offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified at their coming into being. Now, in any event, the fetus is not consecrated, and he slaughtered the mother inside, in the courtyard: is the offspring a non-sacred animal [slaughtered] in the courtyard, and he is liable, since the fetus was not consecrated, or not?

notes.dh: ולמאן דאמר וולדי קדשים בהווייתן הן קדושים
notes.he: בשעת לידתן ולאו ממעי אימן [הם] הכי נמי (הכא גבי חולין אמרינן דלא הוי הולד חולין) [מי אמרינן האי לא הוי חולין] אלא משעת הוויית לידתן או דילמא גבי חולין אפי' ממעי אימן הוי חולין וליחייב:
notes.en: And according to the one who says offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified at their coming into being: At the time of their birth and not [from] their mother’s womb. [Do we say this offspring is non-sacred] only from the time of their coming into being at birth, or perhaps with regard to non-sacred status it is non-sacred even in its mother’s womb, and he would be liable?
